Forward `set_resource` through every exporter wrapper\n148\t\n149\tImplement `set_resource` on all four resilient wrappers, delegating to the inner\n150\texporter. The wrappers hold `inner: Arc<...>`; the SDK calls `set_resource` at\n151\tprovider-build time while the `Arc` is still unique, so `Arc::get_mut` is the\n152\tdelegation mechanism. A wrapper that cannot obtain the unique reference must log\n153\tat WARN rather than fail silently — a silently resource-less exporter is exactly\n154\tthe failure being fixed.\n155\t\n156\t**Rule adopted going forward:** any wrapper interposed on an OTel SDK exporter\n157\ttrait must implement *every* method of that trait explicitly, including ones\n158\twith defaulted no-op bodies. Defaulted trait methods are the trap; `export()`\n159\talone is never a complete implementation.\n160\t\n161\t### 2. Identity that changes belongs on the record, not the Resource\n162\t\n163\t| Attribute | Layer | Rationale |\n164\t|---|---|---|\n165\t| `service.name`, `service.version`, `service.instance.id`, `service.namespace` | Resource | Fixed for the process |\n166\t| `host.name`, `process.pid`, `needle.session_id` | Resource | Fixed for the process |\n167\t| `deployment.cluster`, `needle.worker.pool` (config `resource_attributes`) | Resource | Fixed for the host |\n168\t| `needle.agent`, `needle.model` | Resource **and** record | Resource carries the configured default; the record carries the adapter/model actually dispatched, which routing can change per bead |\n169\t| `workspace` (repo basename) | **Record** | Changes every time the worker roams; a Resource value is structurally incapable of being correct |\n170\t\n171\t### 3. Populate `TelemetryEvent.workspace` at emit time\n172\t\n173\t`Telemetry` gains a current-workspace cell that the worker updates when a claim\n174\tbinds it to a workspace. `emit`/`emit_sync` read that cell instead of writing\n175\t`None`. `Bead.workspace` (`src/claim/mod.rs:609`) is already the authoritative\n176\tsource and is known before dispatch, so no new plumbing crosses a module\n177\tboundary. Basename-only reduction stays where `519468a` put it, in\n178\t`workspace_label`, so full filesystem paths still never reach the browser.\n179\t\n180\t### 4. Assert on exported records, not on builder output\n181\t\n182\tEvery telemetry-attribute test must run through the real\n183\t`build_http_providers` / `build_grpc_providers` path with a capturing exporter\n184\tsubstituted at the transport seam, and assert on the Resource and attributes the\n185\texporter is handed. `519468a`'s `test_exported_log_record_contains_service_version`\n186\tis the right shape and the wrong depth — it swaps in a bare\n187\t`SdkLoggerProvider`, bypassing the wrapper that is the actual defect.\n188\t\n189\t### 5. Verification is a wire capture, not a green test\n190\t\n191\tThe exit criterion for this work is a raw OTLP payload captured from a real\n192\t`needle` binary containing the expected resource attributes, plus a live\n193\tdashboard snapshot with no `null` in `repo`, `harness`, `model`, `semver`, or\n194\t`worker_pool`. The isolated-capture harness used to produce Evidence 2 above is\n195\tcheap, safe against the live fleet, and should be checked in as a script.\n196\t\n197\t## Consequences\n198\t\n199\t**Positive**\n200\t- The dashboard's worker card becomes accurate rather than decorative, and\n201\t  `Repo` tracks a roaming worker instead of freezing at its launch workspace.\n202\t- Traces to Tempo regain service identity — currently every NEEDLE span lands\n203\t  with an empty Resource, which makes them near-unusable for correlation.\n204\t- VictoriaLogs' configured stream fields (`service.name`, `deployment.cluster`,\n205\t  `service.instance.id`) start receiving two of three from NEEDLE rather than\n206\t  relying entirely on collector upserts.\n207\t- `needle.worker.pool` and every other operator-supplied\n208\t  `telemetry.otlp.resource_attributes` entry begin working for the first time;\n209\t  they are currently silently discarded.\n210\t\n211\t**Negative / accepted**\n212\t- A per-record `workspace` attribute is one more attribute on every log record.\n213\t  Cardinality is bounded by the repo count under `workspace_root` (tens), and it\n214\t  is a basename, not a path.\n215\t- Adding `needle.agent`/`needle.model` at both layers means two sources for one\n216\t  concept. The record value wins; the Resource value documents the configured\n217\t  default. This is stated in the semantic mapping so consumers do not guess.\n218\t- The dashboard server's `normalize_otlp_log` fallback chain\n219\t  (record → body → resource) already implements exactly this precedence, so no\n220\t  coordinated deployment is required — NEEDLE can ship first.\n221\t\n222\t**Neutral**\n223\t- No change to the `Sink` trait, the file sink, the JSONL format, or the browser\n224\t  contract's shape. `schema_version` on the dashboard contract stays where it is;\n225\t  fields that were always specified simply stop being `null`.\n226\t\n227\t## Alternatives Considered\n228\t\n229\t### Put the workspace on the Resource and restart the worker on roam\n230\t\n231\tRejected. It would make `Repo` correct by making the worker disposable, throwing\n232\taway the session, its trace context, and its warm state on every hop between\n233\trepos. The roaming design (ADR-004) exists precisely so a worker can drain\n234\tseveral repos in one session.\n235\t\n236\t### Have the collector derive `repo` from `service.instance.id`\n237\t\n238\tRejected. The worker id is `{agent}-{identifier}` — `claude-code-glm-4.7-armor-1`\n239\t— where the identifier is a NATO/operator label that only *usually* resembles a\n240\trepo name. `luna-commitgraph` and `seam-2` parse plausibly; `alpha`, `rota-1`,\n241\tand `otelprobe` do not. Inferring identity from a name string in the collector\n242\twould produce confidently wrong values and move the logic away from the only\n243\tcomponent that actually knows the answer.\n244\t\n245\t### Drop the resilient wrappers and use the OTLP exporters directly\n246\t\n247\tRejected. The wrappers implement the drop-detection and consecutive-failure\n248\taccounting that feeds `telemetry.otlp.dropped` — real operational signal. The\n249\tdefect is a missing trait method, not the wrapper pattern.\n250\t\n251\t### Fix only the exporter wrappers and ship\n252\t\n253\tRejected as insufficient. It would populate `harness`, `model`, `semver`, and\n254\t`worker_pool`, and would populate `Repo` with the boot-time workspace — which,\n255\tfor a roaming fleet, is wrong for most workers most of the time. Populate `TelemetryEvent.workspace` at emit time\n\n`Telemetry` gains a current-workspace cell that the worker updates when a claim\nbinds it to a workspace. `emit`/`emit_sync` read that cell instead of writing\n`None`. `Bead.workspace` (`src/claim/mod.rs:609`) is already the authoritative\nsource and is known before dispatch, so no new plumbing crosses a module\nboundary. Basename-only reduction stays where `519468a` put it, in\n`workspace_label`, so full filesystem paths still never reach the browser.\n\n### 4. Assert on exported records, not on builder output\n\nEvery telemetry-attribute test must run through the real\n`build_http_providers` / `build_grpc_providers` path with a capturing exporter\nsubstituted at the transport seam, and assert on the Resource and attributes the\nexporter is handed. `519468a`'s `test_exported_log_record_contains_service_version`\nis the right shape and the wrong depth — it swaps in a bare\n`SdkLoggerProvider`, bypassing the wrapper that is the actual defect.\n\n### 5. Verification is a wire capture, not a green test\n\nThe exit criterion for this work is a raw OTLP payload captured from a real\n`needle` binary containing the expected resource attributes, plus a live\ndashboard snapshot with no `null` in `repo`, `harness`, `model`, `semver`, or\n`worker_pool`. The isolated-capture harness used to produce Evidence 2 above is\ncheap, safe against the live fleet, and should be checked in as a script.\n\n## Consequences\n\n**Positive**\n- The dashboard's worker card becomes accurate rather than decorative, and\n  `Repo` tracks a roaming worker instead of freezing at its launch workspace.\n- Traces to Tempo regain service identity — currently every NEEDLE span lands\n  with an empty Resource, which makes them near-unusable for correlation.\n- VictoriaLogs' configured stream fields (`service.name`, `deployment.cluster`,\n  `service.instance.id`) start receiving two of three from NEEDLE rather than\n  relying entirely on collector upserts.\n- `needle.worker.pool` and every other operator-supplied\n  `telemetry.otlp.resource_attributes` entry begin working for the first time;\n  they are currently silently discarded.\n\n**Negative / accepted**\n- A per-record `workspace` attribute is one more attribute on every log record.\n  Cardinality is bounded by the repo count under `workspace_root` (tens), and it\n  is a basename, not a path.\n- Adding `needle.agent`/`needle.model` at both layers means two sources for one\n  concept. The record value wins; the Resource value documents the configured\n  default. This is stated in the semantic mapping so consumers do not guess.\n- The dashboard server's `normalize_otlp_log` fallback chain\n  (record → body → resource) already implements exactly this precedence, so no\n  coordinated deployment is required — NEEDLE can ship first.\n\n**Neutral**\n- No change to the `Sink` trait, the file sink, the JSONL format, or the browser\n  contract's shape. `schema_version` on the dashboard contract stays where it is;\n  fields that were always specified simply stop being `null`.\n\n## Alternatives Considered\n\n### Put the workspace on the Resource and restart the worker on roam\n\nRejected. It would make `Repo` correct by making the worker disposable, throwing\naway the session, its trace context, and its warm state on every hop between\nrepos. The roaming design (ADR-004) exists precisely so a worker can drain\nseveral repos in one session.\n\n### Have the collector derive `repo` from `service.instance.id`\n\nRejected. The worker id is `{agent}-{identifier}` — `claude-code-glm-4.7-armor-1`\n— where the identifier is a NATO/operator label that only *usually* resembles a\nrepo name. `luna-commitgraph` and `seam-2` parse plausibly; `alpha`, `rota-1`,\nand `otelprobe` do not. Inferring identity from a name string in the collector\nwould produce confidently wrong values and move the logic away from the only\ncomponent that actually knows the answer.\n\n### Drop the resilient wrappers and use the OTLP exporters directly\n\nRejected. The wrappers implement the drop-detection and consecutive-failure\naccounting that feeds `telemetry.otlp.dropped` — real operational signal. The\ndefect is a missing trait method, not the wrapper pattern.\n\n### Fix only the exporter wrappers and ship\n\nRejected as insufficient. It would populate `harness`, `model`, `semver`, and\n`worker_pool`, and would populate `Repo` with the boot-time workspace — which,\nfor a roaming fleet, is wrong for most workers most of the time. Root Cause C\nmust be addressed in the same phase or the dashboard trades a blank field for a\nmisleading one.\n","numLines":258,"startLine":1,"totalLines":258}}}
